title: Edge replay-aware metering fence and rate-limiter for retry-safe billing
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers are seeing sporadic double-billing when requests are retried by clients or network intermediaries (at-least-once delivery). Retries originate at the edge (CDN/mobile SDKs), transit layers, and from the SDKs themselves. Existing ledgering and fingerprint propagation reduce cases but do not cover high-throughput edge retries and partial timeouts where duplicate usage is committed before de-duplication completes.

Goal: Implement an edge-friendly, server-sided deduplication \"metering fence\" that integrates with rate limiting and quota accounting to prevent duplicate billing from transient retries while preserving low latency and availability. The solution must be compatible with hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and integrate with current consumption ledger semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Edge-generated idempotency token accepted by ingest within 10ms median overhead
Duplicate billing rate drops to <0.01% on simulated high-retry workload (10k rps with 3% retry rate)
No increased tail latency >5% for 99th percentile across canary traffic
Meters and quota counters never count the same logical request twice when idempotency token matches and metadata aligns
Graceful fallback: when dedupe cache unreachable, the system falls back to current ledger semantics and emits telemetry for reconciliation
technical_design_summary:
We will add a short-lived, server-side idempotency cache (metering fence) keyed by (customer_id, idempotency_key) with a configurable lease window. Edge SDKs/agents will attach a cryptographic opaque idempotency token per logical request. The ingestion path will: 1) check local per-node L1 cache (in-memory), 2) consult a strongly-consistent distributed store for recent tokens (regional Redis with single-writer per customer shard via consistent hashing) when L1 miss, 3) if token is new, reserve a billing lease (soft commit) and proceed; if token seen, return cached response/ack without incrementing counters.

To scale: approximate eviction via TTL and batched compaction to reduce storage. For very high-cardinality customers, we will use a capped LRU sketch + bloom-guided fast-path to reduce roundtrips. Persistent ledger writes remain authoritative for final reconciliation; the metering fence prevents duplicate increments during the critical window between request acceptance and ledger commit.

Trade-offs considered: strong consistency vs latency. We chose a regional strong-path for per-customer fencing to avoid cross-region races while keeping latency within SLOs. We accept a small reconciliation job for any mismatches discovered in async ledger reconciliation. We deliberately avoid global locks to keep throughput.

Security: idempotency tokens are opaque HMACs signed with per-customer key rotated by KMS. Tokens carry a short TTL and nonce to prevent replay beyond lease window.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated implementation in ingest service (default off)
Internal canary: route 1% of internal test traffic + synthetic retry scenarios in staging
Dedicated canary for a subset of customers with high retry rates (opt-in), monitor billing delta and latency
Progressively increase to 25%/50%/100% with automated rollback on safety signals
Final rollout to hosted customers with documentation and SDK updates
implementation_notes: Storage choices considered: Redis (regional), Bigtable (global eventual), Dynamo-style strongly consistent write path. We will implement Redis regional shards for faster parity with existing token caches.
Edge SDK change: add optional header X-RW-Idempotency with opaque HMAC token; SDKs will generate tokens by default in next minor release
Server-side: new middleware in ingest path 'metering-fence' executed before quota decrement. Owned by billing-team in ingest repo.
Backfill: reconciliation job to scan last-72h ledger vs fence logs for audit and correction
Docs: Confluence doc at confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Edge+Idempotency will be the source of truth for operators
